blocks.html: If the laws have found it bad to suborn and corrupt a slave (who is esteemed less than nothing, and as a dead person a) in order to lead him astray and turn him from the service of his master b, with much greater reason [have they found it bad] to spoil and seduce, by gifts, presents, blandishments, promises and other such enticements, a free and freeborn person, and above all one so closely joined as a wife or a child c, dearer beyond comparison to the husband or to the father than all the most precious things in the world d.

notes.citation: Digest 50.17.32 (De diversis regulis iuris antiqui, l. Quod attinet) and Digest 50.17.209 (l. Servitutem)
notes.original: l, quod attinet. ſeruitutẽ. D. de reg. iur.
notes.gloss: Ulpian: as regards the civil law, slaves are held as nobodies; and: we almost compare slavery to death.

notes.citation: Digest 11.3.1 (De servo corrupto, l. 1) and the other laws of the same title
notes.original: l. j. & autres au meſme rittre. D. de ſer. cor.
notes.gloss: The praetor's edict giving an action in double against one who harbours another's slave or persuades him to his harm; rittre = titre.

notes.citation: Code 9.20 (Ad legem Faviam de plagiariis), l. Si (fragment not identified; the print's "Falc." is a slip for the lex Favia or Fabia, since the lex Falcidia concerns legacies); Digest 11.3 (De servo corrupto), l. Et tantum, § 1 (fragment not identified; the title's extension of the action to a son or daughter in power is the point)
notes.original: l. ſi. C. ad I. Falc. de plag. l. & tantum P. j. D. de ſcr. cer.

notes.citation: Digest 4.2.8.3 (Quod metus causa gestum erit, l. Isti quidem, Paul: nihil interest in se quis veritus sit an in liberis suis)
notes.original: l. iſti quidem. D. quod met. can.
notes.gloss: Cited for the rule that fear inflicted through one's children counts as fear to oneself, children being dearer to a parent than anything.
